hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with transient focal neurological deficit (unilateral weakness, aphasia, visual field defect) resolving completely within 24 hours (typically <1 hour). Exam reveals carotid bruit on the right. TIA is a neurological emergency — 10-15% risk of stroke within 90 days, highest in first 48 hours. ABCD2 score predicts stroke risk. Workup: non-contrast head CT (rule out hemorrhage), carotid duplex ultrasound (identify stenosis — this patient has right carotid bruit), ECG (atrial fibrillation is common cause), echocardiogram (cardioembolic source), MRI brain (DWI for ischemia). Labs: CBC, BMP, lipids, HbA1c, PT/PTT. Treatment: antiplatelet therapy — aspirin 81-325mg + clopidogrel (dual antiplatelet for 21 days then single agent), or aspirin + dipyridamole. If carotid stenosis >70%: CEA (carotid endarterectomy). If atrial fibrillation: anticoagulation (DOAC or warfarin). Aggressive risk factor management: statin, BP control, diabetes control, smoking cessation. Admit for expedited workup.
